Check that a prior string is a single distribution call

Source: R/utils-priors.R
is_prior_string.Rd

Accepts one call to an allowlisted distribution whose arguments are all finite numeric constants, such as "normal(0, 1)" or "student_t(3, 0, 2.5)". Statement separators, braces, target increments, nested calls (reject(), exp()), constant(), and symbols are rejected. With class, the distribution must suit that parameter class: location families for b and Intercept; student_t, normal, exponential, gamma, inv_gamma, cauchy for scale classes (brms adds the lower bound); lkj for cor; and normal or uniform for ar and ma, whose location must lie inside [-1, 1] and, for uniform, both bounds as well.

Usage

is_prior_string(x, class = NULL)

Arguments

x

Prior string.

class

Optional brms parameter class.

Value

Logical scalar.

Details

Each distribution takes its own number of arguments, and scale, degrees of freedom, shape, rate, and eta arguments must be positive: normal(mu, sigma), student_t(nu, mu, sigma), cauchy(mu, sigma), skew_normal(xi, omega, alpha), logistic(mu, sigma), double_exponential(mu, sigma), exponential(rate), gamma(a, b), inv_gamma(a, b), lkj(eta), lkj_corr_cholesky(eta), and uniform(a, b) with a < b. uniform is accepted only with class "ar" or "ma"; without class or for any other class it is rejected. Numbers must be plain decimals (optionally with an exponent); hexadecimal or L-suffixed literals, comments, and line breaks are rejected.

Examples

is_prior_string("normal(0, 1)")
#> [1] TRUE
is_prior_string("student_t(3, 0, 2.5)", class = "sd")
#> [1] TRUE
is_prior_string("normal(0, -1)")
#> [1] FALSE
is_prior_string("uniform(-1, 1)", class = "ar")
#> [1] TRUE
